- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then sharply decline, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — forecasts drift toward historical lows after initial spikes, but not fast enough to match true price corrections.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 2–5 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, leading to premature price stabilization.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in the first 5–7 days, then gradually correct — but not always in sync with true price behavior.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks, especially when true prices drop below 65–68.
